messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Severity=high - Serving group `inference-prod` is emitting elevated OOMs and elevated p99 latency on kv-cache backed routes. Alert rule: kv_cache.oom_rate > 5% for 3m. Auto-paged to oncall.

oncall-alex: I'm on it. Popping into metrics now. Which pool? Any customer-facing tickets? :coffee:

sre-maya: Looks like it's the `kv-cache-v2` allocator on gpus in us-west1. Error spikes at 17:05UTC, correlates with a deployment spike ~17:03 where continuous-batching rollout hit 60% traffic. Some workers show fragmentation -> slow cudaMalloc and OOMs.

eng-ml-raj: I see traces where a single request pattern with long context + many cached prefixes pushed the kv cache live size above normal and allocator fragmentation prevented reuse. Likely caused by a new batching config that increases max_batch_tokens and increases prefetch.

support-lina: CS reports 3 paying customers experiencing increased tail latencies and a few timeouts. They see 503s on generate calls between 17:05-17:18. I've opened tickets and flagged priority.

oncall-alex: Immediate mitigations we can do: 1) revert or scale down continuous-batching rollout to previous config OR 2) force disable kv prefix caching for heavy routes OR 3) apply allocator env tweak (PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF) and restart subset of workers. Which is lowest-risk?

eng-runtime-kevin: Low-risk fastest: roll back batching config to previous stable and scale up a few spare nodes to soak traffic. Rollback will stop creating the large transient allocations. We can also hotpatch env to set `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:128,garbage_collection_threshold:0.6` to reduce fragmentation, but that requires rolling restarts of workers.

oncall-alex: I'll roll back the batching rollout to 10% immediately. Deploy-bot, can you pin inference-config/batching to v1.14 and trigger rollout? 

deploy-bot: Received. Patching rollout for config `inference-config/batching` -> set rollout:10% (was 60%). Starting canary rollback. See: https://deploys.internal/r/12345

sre-maya: Good. Also increasing node count by +2 in us-west1 autoset so that existing healthy nodes can pick up traffic while we stabilize.

eng-ml-raj: If rollback doesn't cut it, next step is to disable kv prefix caching for routes with context > 8k tokens. Quick toggle is `kv_cache.enabled=false` via config override per route.

support-lina: Noted. CS will tell affected customers that we're mitigating and will follow up with timeline.

(10m later)

oncall-alex: Rollback to 10% applied. Early signs: OOMs down 80% on rolled-back pods. But we still see a tail of fragmentation-related OOMs on a subset of nodes that didn't rotate yet.

eng-runtime-kevin: For those nodes we should do a rolling restart, but staggered. Command to restart deployment workers (one at a time):
```
kubectl rollout restart deployment/inference-worker -n prod --field-selector metadata.name=inference-worker-<pod-id>
```
We'll script sleep 60s between pods.

sre-maya: I'm running a one-off script to drain and cordon the worst offenders then restart runtime process to free CUDA arenas. Using:
```
kubectl exec -it <pod> -n prod -- bash -lc "kill -HUP 1 || pkill -f inference_worker && sleep 10 && /usr/local/bin/inference_worker &"
```
That should trigger freeing of GPU memory and reinit cuda context.

eng-ml-raj: We're also pushing a hotpatch to env: `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:128,garbage_collection_threshold:0.6` as an experiment on a small subset (2 pods). This reduces allocator split size and encourages larger chunks to be freed.

oncall-alex: Go for the hotpatch on 2 pods only. Tag them as canary.

deploy-bot: Applied env patch to `inference-worker` canary pods: inference-worker-canary-1, inference-worker-canary-2.

(20m later)

eng-ml-raj: Canary pods with the PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF change show much lower fragmentation symptoms. cudaMalloc latency decreased, and live set stabilized. No customer 503s tied to those canaries.

sre-maya: OOM count across cluster is down ~92% vs peak. Rolling restarts continuing; we have ~12 pods left to restart across us-west1.

support-lina: CS informed customers and one customer (acct: acme-inc) confirmed retries are working. They want a postmortem and ETA for full fix.

oncall-alex: Current action items: continue rolling restarts (sre team), apply env hotpatch cluster-wide after restarts if stable (eng runtime/infra), verify batching rollback keeps traffic stable (eng runtime), and schedule postmortem.

eng-runtime-kevin: Agreed. I'm preparing a cluster-wide rollout for PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF after rolling restarts finish. Also adding MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=4 for CPU processes to reduce host fragmentation (non-gpu components). We'll coordinate a 15-minute maintenance window to minimize risk.

eng-ml-raj: Follow-ups for product: add a canary test that runs realistic long-context workload to trigger kv cache growth and detect allocator fragmentation before rollout. Also add telemetry measuring allocator fragmentation metrics (free segments count, largest free chunk) and expose in dashboards.

sre-maya: I'll own the postmortem and timeline. Immediate blameless notes: rollout speed + config change increased memory churn; allocator heuristics didn't cope with heavier long-context workloads.

cs-jordan: I'll draft customer comms for affected accounts with incident summary, remediation steps taken, and next steps.

support-lina: Customers impacted (observed): acme-inc, beta-studio, healthapp-prod. All have open tickets. No data loss reported; just increased latency/timeouts.

(45m later)

deploy-bot: Rolling restarts complete for us-west1. All pods show healthy: 50/50 traffic split stable. No new OOMs after last restart.

oncall-alex: Marking incident as mitigated for now. We'll keep monitoring for 2 hours. Thanks everyone for fast coordination. :tada:

eng-ml-raj: Postmortem items (short): 1) Add allocator fragmentation telemetry + alert 2) Add long-context canary test to CI 3) Harden batching rollout strategy: slower ramp + automated fallback if kv cache grows >50% 4) Document PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF recommendation and include in private deployment docs.

sre-maya: Also adding an action to validate glibc arena settings in our runtime images: set `MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=4` and evaluate CPU memory fragmentation impact in staging.

oncall-alex: I'll update the incident channel thread with timeline and final customer comms link once CS finishes.

cs-jordan: Customer comms sent to affected accounts. Will attach to postmortem.

(1h later)

oncall-alex: Closing loop. Incident moved to postmortem state. Thanks all. If anyone has anything to add to the timeline, drop it here.

eng-runtime-kevin: Noted. I'm going to schedule the cluster-wide rollout of the PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF hotpatch during low-traffic window tomorrow and will include a rollback plan.

sre-maya: POSTMORTEM OWNER: @sre-maya. ETA for writeup: 48 hours.
